## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-fascicle Vinaya manual on the canonical handling of *sānshuǐ* 三水 ("three waters") in Buddhist monastic practice by **Yìjìng** 義淨 ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8), 635–713). Author signature: *唐三藏法師義淨撰*.

**Abstract**

The *Sānshuǐ yàoxíng fǎ* is the most canonical of Yìjìng's three short Vinaya manuals (with [KR6k0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0188) and [KR6k0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0190)) and represents his programmatic application of South-Asian *Mūlasarvāstivāda*-Vinaya practice to Chinese monastic life. As the *Vinaya* manual that Yìjìng dispatched on the canonical handling of drinking and ritual water, the work supplements the larger *Nánhǎi jìguī nèifǎ zhuàn* 南海寄歸內法傳 (T2125), where Yìjìng's broader programme of *Mūlasarvāstivāda*-correction of Chinese practice is set out. The text is precisely keyed to Indian Buddhist hot-climate pragmatics — water purification, mid-day meal restrictions, the use of strained water from the *lùshuǐnáng* 漉水囊 (water-strainer) — that had no exact Chinese antecedents and required his explicit pedagogical attention. Composition belongs to Yìjìng's post-695 Luòyáng / Chángān decades.
